Strong community engagement was at the heart of our recent Farm Waste Recycling event, delivered in partnership with Plasback NZ.

By working alongside the rural community and providing a service that fits how farmers operate, Manawatū District Council helped create a practical, accessible way for farmers to engage on their terms.

Over two days:
👉 74 farmers took part, 
👉 recycling 190 Plasback liners of bale wrap and silage stack covers, 
👉 to divert nearly 42 tonnes of plastic from landfill. 

The event shows the value of meeting people where they are. By focusing on solutions that are simple, relevant, and useful, we’re able to strengthen connections with our rural sector while supporting better environmental outcomes.

Funded through the waste levy received by Council from the Ministry for the Environment, the initiative was delivered at no cost to ratepayers and provided financial benefits back to farmers.

A genuine team effort, with thanks to Plasback NZ, CNH, Transag, The Glob, Maskills, Manfeild Park Trust, and the Feilding Agricultural High School Girls 1st XV rugby team for their support.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">💧 A new identity for an essential service💧

As Manawatū Water continues to evolve as Manawatū District Council's dedicated in-house water services business unit, we've introduced a new visual identity that reflects its role while keeping the customer experience simple.

Developed to work alongside the MDC brand, the identity creates a consistent and recognisable presence for Manawatū Water across our website, projects and communications. Importantly, residents continue to access everything through the familiar Manawatū District Council website.

As General Manager Infrastructure <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/hamish-waugh-a0890b28?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Hamish Waugh</a> explains:
"People shouldn't have to work out which organisation they need to contact. Keeping Manawatū Water within the Council website makes it simple for customers, while the dedicated branding helps people easily recognise information relating to water services."

This project was developed entirely in-house from the brand strategy and visual identity through to the website integration, templates and supporting collateral. It reflects the capability within our organisation and what can be achieved when communications, design and operational teams work together to create something that's both practical and purposeful.

💧 Explore the carousel to discover the thinking behind the new identity and see how those principles have shaped the Manawatū Water brand.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">42 tonnes of farm plastics diverted from landfill ♻️ 

Strong community engagement was at the heart of our recent Farm Waste Recycling event, delivered in partnership with <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/plasback-nz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Plasback NZ</a>.

Over two days:
👉 74 farmers took part, 
👉 recycling 190 Plasback liners of bale wrap and silage stack covers, 
👉 to divert nearly 42 tonnes of plastic from landfill.

Funded through the waste levy received by Council from the Ministry for the Environment, the initiative was delivered at no cost to ratepayers and provided financial benefits back to farmers.
